localChanges: chore: lock the engine packages that teach Settlers to build roads between cities and clean up pollution

log: A `product` rule (1 when nothing matches) that scales how keen a computer player's workers are to clean up pollution (civ-clone/web-renderer#366).

`PollutionConcern` rules: Civilized 1.5, Friendly 1.25, Militaristic and Aggressive 0.75, multiplied together (civ-clone/web-renderer#366). v474.05's AI cleans pollution whatever the leader; the weighting is ours. Needs base-leader-personality 0.1.1.

civ1TerrainPolicy finds the cheapest way between each city and its two nearest neighbours within ten squares (civ-clone/web-renderer#384), within an ellipse around the pair, preferring straight lines between equal costs, and offers a Road on each tile of it (worth 1), then a Railroad once Railroad is known. The way is cached per player per turn, and its tiles join the policy's job tiles.
Once Railroad is known, a Road's value includes what the Railroad it allows would add, so a Road goes down on a River where the Road alone adds nothing (civ-clone/web-renderer#385).

Polluted tiles get a cleanPollution job, valued by the yields the pollution costs (weighted as other jobs), plus 1, plus a quarter for each other polluted tile the player has, times the leader's PollutionConcern (base-leader-personality 0.1.1; civ-clone/web-renderer#366).

The policy now wants a terrain worker for every six cities rather than eight: in the arena, with routes to build, one for every six gave more linked cities on both seed sets and nothing worse; one for every four founded fewer cities (civ-clone/web-renderer#234).
